case_name: Roshni And Another vs State Of Punjab And Others

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Roshni and another (girl aged 17 years 11 months and boy aged 28 years)

facts_of_case: Petitioner No.1, a minor girl, and petitioner No.2, a boy, are in love and got married against their parents' wishes. They claim threats to kill them from private respondents.

legal_principles.principle: Assuming a consensual relationship, the parties are entitled to protection of their life and liberty as envisaged under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
legal_principles.held: Assuming the petitioners were in a consensual relationship, without having got married, they would still be entitled to protection of their life and liberty as envisaged under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

legal_principles.principle: The minimum ages for a bridegroom and a bride are essential conditions of Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: A perusal of Section 5, ibid leaves no manner of doubt that one of the essential conditions of Hindu Marriage Act is that the bridegroom must be above 21 years and the bride above 18 years.

outcome.final_order: Grant of appropriate protection to the petitioners qua their life and liberty as apprehended by them for the reasons stated hereinafter.
